blocked.status: BLOCKED (B-SRC: SRC-008; B-Q: Q-001; B-MET: AC-FR-004-1 depends on Q-001)

acs.text: Given the extensions `toc` and `attr_list` and the issue's example document (`# Guide`, `## Contents {: .no-toc }`, `[TOC]`, `## Install`, `## Usage`), when it is converted, then the output contains `href="#guide"`, `href="#install"` and `href="#usage"` and does not contain `href="#contents"`.
Given the same document, when it is converted, then `md.toc` contains `href="#install"` and does not contain `Contents`.
Given the same document with `{: .no-toc }` removed from the "Contents" heading, when it is converted, then the output contains `href="#contents"`.
Given the issue's example document with `toc` and `attr_list`, when it is converted, then the output contains `id="contents"` on the `h2` element whose text is `Contents`.
Given two headings `## Contents {: .no-toc }` and `## Contents` in one document, when it is converted, then the two headings have different `id` values and neither is empty.
Given `## Contents {: .no-toc #custom }`, when it is converted, then the heading has `id="custom"`.

Given the issue's example document with `toc` and `attr_list`, when it is converted, then `md.toc_tokens` has one top-level entry with `id` equal to `guide`, and its `children` list holds entries with `id` equal to `install` and `usage`, in that order.
Given the same document, when it is converted, then no entry anywhere in `md.toc_tokens` has `id` equal to `contents`.
Given a document with the `toc` extension and no `no-toc` class, when it is converted, then `md.toc_tokens` and `md.toc` are identical to the output before this change.

questions.title: Should the class name be configurable, and under what option name?
questions.question: Should the `toc` extension get a configuration option for the excluded-heading class name?
questions.options: (a) No, fixed `no-toc` only (b) Yes, new option (name to be given by maintainer) (c) Other

questions.title: Sub-headings of an excluded heading
questions.question: If an excluded heading has deeper headings below it, should those be listed in `md.toc_tokens` and the TOC, and under which parent?
questions.options: (a) Listed, attached to the nearest listed parent (b) Excluded together with their parent (c) Other
questions.blocks: none (no criterion in this spec covers it)

questions.title: Permalinks and anchor links on excluded headings
questions.question: With `permalink` or `anchorlink` enabled, should an excluded heading still get the link?

questions.title: Several classes on one heading
questions.question: Should `## Contents {: .no-toc .other }` be excluded?
questions.options: (a) Yes, any class token matches (b) Only when `no-toc` is the sole class (c) Other

criteria.reason: The extensions, the exact example document and the exact substrings to find or exclude in the output are all given.
The action (convert, then read md.toc) and the exact substring checks (contains href="#install", does not contain "Contents") are stated.
The document variant with the no-toc class removed is fully specified and the expected substring href="#contents" is exact.
The document and the expected outcome (id="contents" on the h2 whose text is Contents) are stated exactly enough to assert.
Both headings are given, and the checks (different id values, neither empty) are concrete comparisons on the parsed ids.
The heading source `## Contents {: .no-toc #custom }` and the exact expected attribute id="custom" are stated.
The expected toc_tokens structure is fully specified: one top-level id guide, with children install and usage in that order.
The check that no entry anywhere in md.toc_tokens has id contents is a concrete, exact assertion on a public attribute.
The document is unspecified ("a document") and the expected value is 'the output before this change', a baseline that is not written in the criterion, so no exact expected outcome can be asserted.
